facts.text: Lincoln was originally called La Placita del Rio Bonito by Hispanic settlers in the 1850s before adopting the name Lincoln in 1869 when the county was created.
The town sits on the Bonito Valley, a site whose prehistory and history are interpreted through 17 preserved structures at the Lincoln Historic Site.
Lincoln Historic Site is the most visited state historic site in New Mexico, showcasing 17 adobe and stone buildings that trace the Lincoln County War of the 1870s.
The Anderson-Freeman Visitor Center displays a timeline from American Indian prehistory to the Lincoln County War, highlighting figures like Billy the Kid and Pat Garrett.
During World War II, the abandoned Old Raton Ranch camp outside Lincoln housed Japanese American railroad workers and their families for about a year.
The Old Lincoln County Courthouse, now a museum, once served as a store, residence, Masonic lodge, courthouse, and jail, reflecting the town’s layered history.
